messages:
mira: Anyone else seeing a canary FP8 tail-latency regression after last night's coalescer merge? Dashboard link: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/420 — p95 ~4x, p99 ~10x for /generate in us-west-2. model=redwood-fp8-v2, route=/generate :eyes:

alex: Yup, noticed alerts this morning. I thought kernel-selector tweak landed too — could be interplay. Which PRs were in the window?

mira: Coalescer PR (#4821) + microbatch hysteresis change merged at 02:14. Kernel-selector change (#4876) that prefers fused FP8 kernels merged at 02:26. Canary rollout started 02:40.

sam: I'm starting a bisect on the canary commit range now. Will try to reproduce locally with the perf harness (28 concurrency, 256 max_len).

sam: Bisect update: narrows to commit 0f4c8b3 — "coalescer: widen merge window, add hysteresis to microbatch coalescer". Reverting that commit in canary drops p99 back to baseline.

jon: Profiler snapshot from canary (sampling 5s):
```
CPU (worker-thread-3): 34.1% memcpy (dequant copy)
CPU (worker-thread-3): 18.7% dequant_dispatch
GPU queue stall: increased wait on CPU-to-GPU memcpy
KV cache miss rate: 27% -> 68% after coalescer change
Worker sleep wakeups increased by 2.8x
```
Looks like coalescing more heterogeneous requests into the same batches -> more unique KV keys per batch -> colder KV cache -> more dequant paths triggered (we only keep quantized cache entries for hot prefixes). Dequant overhead + memcpys dominate tail.

mira: Repro script I used:
```
./tools/perf_harness --model redwood-fp8-v2 --route /generate --concurrency 28 --seq 256 --prefix-set samples/heterogeneous_prefixes.json
```
Using heterogeneous prefixes is critical to see the effect. Homogeneous prefixes don't regress.

alex: That matches my notes. The coalescer widened window from 4ms->12ms and disabled cross-tenant isolation, so now batches mix request shapes more often. Kernel-selector's fused FP8 kernels are slightly faster for hot-path but require an extra dequant memcpy when inputs are mixed. Combined effect -> worse tail.

jon: Another datapoint: when we force kernel-selector to prefer non-fused int8 path via env var `RW_FORCE_KERNEL=int8_basic`, p95/p99 return to normal despite coalescer change. So it's definitely an interaction.

mira: Suggested mitigations:
- Hotfix: revert coalescer commit 0f4c8b3 on canary (already tested, works).
- Short-term: re-enable tenant isolation in coalescer or narrow merge window to 4ms.
- Longer: update kernel-selector to detect heterogeneous-batch dequant penalty and avoid fused kernels for mixed-shape batches OR keep quantized KV entries for more prefixes (cost tradeoff).

sam: I can open a revert PR for 0f4c8b3 and a follow-up that adds a config flag gating cross-tenant coalescing. Will include perf tests that use heterogeneous prefix sets in CI.

ops: Rolling back canary to previous build now — initiating rollback at 03:12. If rollback is clean we'll pause the wider rollout.

deploy-bot: Rollback started by ops for canary group us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T03:12:04Z.

ci-bot: FYI: CI perf suite flagged this change earlier but only with homogeneous prefixes; new test added to perf suite to exercise heterogeneous prefix mixes. See CI run 7891.

alex: Good catch. Once sam posts the revert PR let's run the updated perf suite and then re-evaluate a gradual rollout with tenant-isolation enabled. :thumbsup:

mira: I'll add reproducer notes and attach the trace artifacts to the revert PR. Thanks everyone.

jon: One more note: KV profiler suggests we should consider tracking per-batch prefix entropy metric in telemetry so kernel-selector/coalescer can make smarter decisions at runtime.

mira: Agreed — adding to backlog as action item.
